title: Why You Forget a Word, Even When It's 'On the Tip of Your Tongue'
hook: That frustrating feeling of almost recalling a word has a name.

narration.text: That frustrating feeling of almost recalling a word has a name.
It is called the Tip of the Tongue phenomenon, or TOT.
Your brain has two main memory systems, semantic and phonological.
Semantic memory stores concepts, meanings, and facts.
Phonological memory stores the actual sounds and pronunciations.
When you experience TOT, your semantic memory has the meaning.
But the link to the phonological memory, the word itself, is temporarily blocked.
It is like your brain knows what it wants to say, but not how to say it.
This often happens with less frequently used words or names.
What word was on the tip of your tongue most recently?

description: Ever felt like you know a word, but just cannot quite say it? This video explains the 'Tip of the Tongue' phenomenon, where your brain's memory systems briefly disconnect. Discover why this common experience happens and what it reveals about how we recall information.
topic: Why you sometimes struggle to recall a word, but feel like it is 'on the tip of your tongue', explaining the Tip of the Tongue phenomenon.
